intro: The past continuous describes an action in progress at a moment in the past: “I was having dinner when you called.” We use it to set the scene in a story and to show that one action interrupted another.
objectifs: Form the past continuous with was / were + -ing, in all forms.
Say what you were doing at a particular time in the past.
Combine the past continuous and the past simple with when and while.
Know when not to use the past continuous (states and past habits).

texte: The past continuous uses the past of “to be” (was / were, lesson 39) + verb-ing. It is the present continuous (lesson 8) moved into the past: I am working → I was working.
Negative: wasn't / weren't + -ing. Question: Was / Were + subject + -ing? Short answers: Yes, I was. / No, they weren't.
sections.note: -ing spelling (the same as the present continuous): make → making, sit → sitting, lie → lying, study → studying.

sections.titre: Use 1: an action in progress at a past time
texte: Use it to say what was happening at a particular time in the past. The action started before that moment and continued after it.
Common time phrases: at 8 o'clock yesterday, at this time last week, all day / all evening, at midnight.
exemples: At 9 p.m. yesterday, I was watching the news.
What were you doing at this time last year?
It was raining all morning in Liège.

sections.titre: Use 2: an interrupted action (when + past simple)
texte: We use the two tenses together: the past continuous for the long action (the background), the past simple for the short action that happens in the middle of it.
“When” usually comes before the short action in the past simple. Use a comma when the when-clause comes first.
exemples: When you called, I was cooking.
I started cooking before you called.
Different meaning: you called, THEN I cooked (one after the other).

sections.titre: Use 3: two actions at the same time (while) and the background
texte: “While” links two long actions that happen at the same time: both are in the past continuous. While can also introduce the long action before a past simple.
At the start of a story, the past continuous describes the scene: what was happening around, before the main event.
exemples: While I was studying, my brother was playing video games.
Two actions at the same time.
While we were waiting for the bus, we met an old friend.
The sun was shining and the birds were singing.

texte: Do not use the past continuous for past habits: use the past simple or “used to” (lesson 44). Do not use it for states (be, have for possession, know, like…): use the past simple.
State verbs (know, like, want, need, believe, belong, understand) do not normally take -ing, in the past or in the present.

lignes: I was reading when he arrived.
On Saturdays I played / used to play football.

formule: was / were + verb-ing · long action (was / were + -ing) + when + short action (past simple)
prononciation: In positive sentences, “was” and “were” are weak: was /wəz/, were /wə/ (UK): I was working /aɪ wəz ˈwɜːkɪŋ/.
In short answers and at the end of a sentence, they are strong: Yes, I was /wɒz/. Yes, we were /wɜː/.
The -ing ending is /ɪŋ/: do not pronounce a hard g at the end.
In “When the phone rang, I was sleeping”, stress the important words: PHONE, RANG, SLEEPing.
erreurs: When I arrived, she was cooking.
I was watching TV when the lights were going out.
I was watching TV when the lights went out.
The short, interrupting action is in the past simple.
When I was child, I was playing outside every day.
When I was a child, I played outside every day.
Past habit: past simple (or used to), not past continuous.
While I cooked, the phone was ringing.
While I was cooking, the phone rang.
Long action: past continuous; short action: past simple.

dialogue.contexte: At a police station in Namur, an officer asks a witness about a small bike accident.
lignes: Can you tell me what happened?
Yes. I was waiting at the bus stop on Rue de Fer.
“What was … like?” asks for a description.
It was raining a little, and a lot of people were crossing the street.
He was riding very fast. He was looking at his phone while he was riding.
No, he wasn't. When the car stopped suddenly, he hit it and fell.
Short answer, then the main events in the past simple.

mots: While I was cooking, he called.

I saw an accident on the way to work.

exercices.consigne: Put the verb in the past continuous.
items: Kofi ___ (study) in the library all afternoon.

exercices.consigne: Choose the correct form of each verb.
items: When the teacher ___ (come) in, the students ___ (talk).
We ___ (watch) a film when the electricity ___ (go) off.
While I ___ (wash) the dishes, my sister ___ (dry) them.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: When he was calling, I was in the shower.
When he called, I was in the shower.
She was drive to work when it happened.
She was driving to work when it happened.

exercices.consigne: Make one sentence with the word in brackets. Choose the right tenses.
items: I was sleeping when you phoned.
It rained. It was cold. (and – describe the scene)
It was raining and it was cold.
She drove home. She heard the news on the radio. (while)
While she was driving home, she heard the news on the radio.
They played. We prepared the meal. (while – same time)
While they were playing, we were preparing the meal.

exercices.consigne: Describe a moment when something unexpected happened. First describe the scene (past continuous), then the event (past simple).
items: Last Friday evening I was sitting on my balcony in Abidjan. The sun was going down and my neighbours were playing music. Suddenly, I heard a loud noise. A big branch fell from the tree onto my neighbour's car! Luckily, nobody was standing near it.

a_retenir: It describes an action in progress at a past time, or the background of a story.
A long action (past continuous) is interrupted by a short one (past simple): I was cooking when you called.
While + two long actions at the same time.
No past continuous for state verbs or past habits (use the past simple or used to).
